name: @stonedogcode/tests
description: A test-inventory surface for a fleet of repositories: how many tests each project has, at which tier, in which language, collected from projects that declare their tiers rather than having them guessed.
author: StoneDogCode L.L.C.
//workspaces: `server` only, and it is private. The `files` list below ships src/ alone, so the standalone server travels with the repository and never with the tarball.
//exports: Three entry points so a consumer importing the table does not drag `node:fs` into a client bundle. `.` is isomorphic (types, schema readers), `./node` is the collector, `./styled` is the React layer and the only one that needs @stonedogcode/style.
//files: Excluding __tests__ is load-bearing, not tidiness. Consumers add `node_modules/@stonedogcode/tests/src/**` to their Panda include globs, so anything under src/ is statically parsed at THEIR build — and the tests import jest globals.

scripts.//dev: The standalone server, in its own workspace so one root `npm install` is enough and react resolves to a single hoisted copy — two Reacts in one tree fail at runtime with 'Invalid hook call', pointing at a component rather than at the install that caused it.
scripts.//test: Jest runs as ESM (see jest.config.cjs), which needs the VM modules flag.
scripts.//collect: The CLI, run in-repo through tsx. There is deliberately no `bin`: this package ships TypeScript SOURCE (Panda needs it), and a `bin` pointing at a .ts file cannot execute on the Node 22 floor this package declares. Consumers call `collect()` from @stonedogcode/tests/node instead — a bin that only works on some of the versions you claim to support is worse than none.
scripts.//collect:fixtures: Regenerate the demo fixtures from real repositories. They are committed so the server and the component tests run against real collected output rather than hand-written mocks.
scripts.//gate: The server is type-checked here too. It is not published, but it is the worked example, and an example that does not compile is worse than none.
scripts.gate: npm run type-check && npm run type-check:server && npm run lint && npm run test && npm run test:integration
scripts.//verify:package: Pack, install the tarball into a temp directory as a consumer, typecheck through the PUBLISHED exports map and then RUN the collector from it. The running is the point: `files`, `exports` and the tarball contents are invisible to a test suite operating on source files in this repo, and they are exactly what breaks at publish time — after review, when the version is already burned.
scripts.//publish:stonedog-tests: Run from a terminal, INTERACTIVELY — npm prompts for the 2FA one-time password and the login flow needs a browser, so an agent cannot complete it. You need not log in first: it starts `npm login` itself if needed. It refuses a checkout that is detached, dirty, not on main, or behind origin/main; refuses a version the registry already has; refuses an account that is not an owner of an existing package (which would fail as a misleading 404); runs the gate and verify:package; then proves the result by installing from the registry.
scripts.//panda:css: The stylesheet itself. `panda codegen` emits the styled-system JS but no CSS; without this the standalone server renders components whose class names have no rules behind them — the exact silent failure the include globs are guarded against.

//dependencies: ZERO runtime dependencies. Globbing is `node:fs/promises`'s own `glob`, which is why the engines floor is 22 rather than the fleet's usual 20 — see below.
//engines: node >=22 because the collector globs with `fs.promises.glob`, added in 22. The React layer alone would run on 20; one engines field cannot say that, and understating it would let an install succeed and the CLI fail.
//peerDependencies: react/react-dom are peers ONLY. Listing them as dependencies too makes npm install a second copy into this package, and two Reacts in one tree fail at runtime with 'Invalid hook call' — a failure that points at the consumer's component, not at this manifest. @stonedogcode/style is optional because `.` and `./node` do not touch it; only `./styled` does.
//publishConfig: A scoped package defaults to RESTRICTED on npm, which requires a paid plan and would fail the publish. Declaring it here means the intent travels with the manifest instead of depending on someone remembering --access public.
